[THOUGHT] The patient is an adolescent with multiple smooth, flesh-colored, dome-shaped papules clustered perinasally and similar periungual/nail-fold papules, plus a history of seizures. This constellation strongly fits tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC): facial angiofibromas (classically perinasal/nasolabial/cheek papules, historically called adenoma sebaceum) and periungual fibromas (Koenen tumors) are major cutaneous features of TSC, and epilepsy is a very common neurologic manifestation from cortical tubers. Other diagnoses that can cause facial papules (e.g., Birt–Hogg–Dubé with fibrofolliculomas) do not typically present with periungual fibromas plus epilepsy in adolescence. Given the clustering of these specific skin findings with seizure history, TSC is the single most likely diagnosis. Consider further evaluation (brain MRI, renal imaging, cardiac/ocular exam, family history/genetic testing) to confirm and assess organ involvement.
